newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles gets a 'county mayor'.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles gets a 'county mayor'.

text.p: There's a new mayor in town.
With little fanfare, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted Tuesday 3-to-2 to change the title of its chairman to "county mayor."
The name change went through over objections from the office of Richard Riordan, mayor of the city of Los Angeles.
"The mayor is the mayor of Los Angeles, and the title of mayor belongs on only one door, the door of Richard Riordan," Riordan's press secretary Noelia Rodriguez said.
The current chairman of the county Board of Supervisors, Michael Antonovich, proposed the name change to enhance the visibility of county government, said Peter Whittingham, Antonovich's spokesman.
"It's more than just cosmetic," Whittingham said. "Very few people know what a supervisor does. Perhaps people now will have a better understanding."
Despite the new, high-profile title, the county mayor will have no new responsibility or power, the county said. Largely ceremonial, the top spot rotates annually among the supervisors.
Supervisor Zev Yaroslavsky, who is in line to become county mayor in December, voted against the change in title.
"He's concerned that it's more perception than reality ... kind of a diversion," Yaroslavsky spokesman Joel Bellman said.
Riordan's office described the name change as superficial. "A rose is a rose is a rose," said spokeswoman Rodriguez.
Los Angeles County, which has 9.3 million residents, provides law enforcement, fire, welfare, health care and other services to residents of 88 cities, including the city of Los Angeles.
The county Board of Supervisors is also the government by default for over one million residents in unincorporated areas.
